adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a contract mismatch. Looking at the diff, GoogleCalendarService.createEvent receives a credentialId parameter and uses it to find the matching destination calendar: `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. However, Office365CalendarService.createEvent at line 72-75 does NOT accept a credentialId parameter and simply destructures the first element: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`. The same pattern exists in LarkCalendarService at line 128. This means for collective team bookings where multiple hosts have different calendars, Office365 and Lark will always use the first (organizer's) calendar regardless of which credential is being used, while Google correctly matches the credential to the appropriate destination calendar.
